nodes.label: F3 - Line thickness advertised but not implemented (beta feature)
nodes.norm_label: f3 - line thickness advertised but not implemented (beta feature)
nodes.rationale: ModeOptions.OptionEnum.LINE_THICKNESS UI/icons/lang exist and documentation promises it, but BuildModeEnum.LINE/DIAGONAL_LINE have the option commented out and Line.getLineBlocks/DiagonalLine.getDiagonalLineBlocks ignore thickness. Spec: thickness t in {1,3,5}, radius r=(t-1)/2, square cross-section for axis-aligned Line, cube neighbourhood for DiagonalLine; keep 1-thick helpers for Wall/Floor and DiagonalWall.

nodes.label: F4 - Diagonal wall has no Fill option (beta feature)
nodes.norm_label: f4 - diagonal wall has no fill option (beta feature)
nodes.rationale: BuildModeEnum.DIAGONAL_WALL has OptionEnum.FILL commented out; DiagonalWall.getDiagonalWallBlocks always fills. Spec: HOLLOW = diagonal line at lowest/highest y plus vertical end columns; FULL = current behaviour.

nodes.label: F7 - 1.21.11 draft features not in 1.21.1 (informational)
nodes.rationale: Fabric-0.19.2-1.21.11 (git-ignored) contains FallbackPreviewRenderer (previews without Catnip) and keybinding categories; noted for a future backport, not part of this work.

nodes.label: Count sync inconsistency (clamped vs unclamped totals)
nodes.norm_label: count sync inconsistency (clamped vs unclamped totals)
nodes.rationale: syncItemCount and the periodic sync send the tier-clamped count while extractBlockFromBackpack sends the unclamped total, causing the HUD to flip between two numbers. Decision: always send the unclamped total; client clamps with the synced max.

nodes.label: NeoForge non-clamping vs Fabric clamping semantics decision
nodes.norm_label: neoforge non-clamping vs fabric clamping semantics decision
nodes.rationale: NeoForge InventoryHelper deliberately does not clamp backpack contributions ('tier only gates access'); Fabric clamps to maxBlocks and reserves one held block as anchor, matching the item tooltip text. Decision: keep these semantics distinct per loader in this round.

nodes.label: RC1 - Worn backpacks never found (CuriosCompatHelper stub)
nodes.norm_label: rc1 - worn backpacks never found (curioscompathelper stub)
nodes.rationale: Fabric CuriosCompatHelper.getBackpacksFromCurios hard-coded to return List.of(), so worn backpacks (Trinkets/Accessories) are invisible to BuildingUpgradeHelper on the server. Fix: enumerate via PlayerInventoryProvider.runOnBackpacks instead.

nodes.label: RC2 - Client validates block availability by introspecting backpack locally
nodes.norm_label: rc2 - client validates block availability by introspecting backpack locally
nodes.rationale: Client builds BackpackWrapper.fromStack on the client where BackpackStorage.clientStorageCopy is rarely populated, so maxFromUpgrade is 0 and BlockSet.encode filters valid entries before the server sees them. Fix: server becomes authoritative, client only reads synced caches.

nodes.label: RC3 - enabled state stored differently from Core, never refreshes type cache
nodes.norm_label: rc3 - enabled state stored differently from core, never refreshes type cache
nodes.rationale: BuildingUpgradeWrapper kept its own enabled field via CUSTOM_DATA and never called refreshWrappersThatImplementAndTypeWrappers(), so UpgradeHandler.getTypeWrappers could keep returning a stale, empty list. Fix: extend UpgradeWrapperBase and drop custom enabled storage; accept that previously-disabled upgrades come back enabled.

nodes.label: F1 - Keybind fallback hard-codes Left Alt (Fabric only)
nodes.norm_label: f1 - keybind fallback hard-codes left alt (fabric only)
nodes.rationale: ClientEvents.isKeybindDown(0) falls back to InputConstants.isKeyDown(window, GLFW_KEY_LEFT_ALT) because KeyMapping.isDown() can desync while a screen is open; a rebound key breaks the fallback. Fix: use KeyBindingHelper.getBoundKeyOf and branch on key type (KEYSYM/SCANCODE vs MOUSE).

nodes.label: F2 - Opening the radial menu cancels an in-progress build
nodes.norm_label: f2 - opening the radial menu cancels an in-progress build
nodes.rationale: FabricClientEvents calls ClientEvents.onGuiOpen() on any screen change including RadialMenu opening, which runs BUILDER_CHAIN.cancel() and discards multi-click builds. Decision: skip cancel for RadialMenu; cancel instead in BuildModes.setBuildMode() only when the mode actually changes.

nodes.label: F8 - Minor: mislabeled tab, TODO in AbstractRandomizerBagItem
nodes.norm_label: f8 - minor: mislabeled tab, todo in abstractrandomizerbagitem
nodes.rationale: SophisticatedBackpacksClientIntegration reuses lang key sophisticatedbuilding.screen.modifier_settings ('Modifier Settings') for the upgrade tab; should have its own key. AbstractRandomizerBagItem carries an out-of-scope TODO to re-enable an item handler capability.

nodes.label: C1: BuilderChain.onLeftClick stale skipFirst bug
nodes.rationale: onLeftClick's survival branch read blocks.skipFirst before this click's assignment (assignment happens later in the same method and BlockSet.setStartPos/clear never reset the flag), and double-subtracted a skipped-first block that was also invalid; fixed by locally computing skipFirst and excluding it explicitly from the valid-entry count.

nodes.label: C2: BreakToolHelper.planClient skipPos parameter for consistency
nodes.norm_label: c2: breaktoolhelper.planclient skippos parameter for consistency
nodes.rationale: planClient gained a nullable skipPos parameter so the client-side plan matches the server's own skipFirst handling exactly, avoiding a mismatch between HUD/preview and actual server behaviour for the Disable-mode first-block skip.

nodes.label: D1: Server-authoritative tool rules
nodes.rationale: Decides per-block which tool breaks it via a common helper (BreakToolHelper + pure ToolSelector), following a strict priority order (unbreakable never, hardness-0 free, effective+correct tool first, main-hand fallback, then hotbar/inventory/offhand/backpack Tool Swapper candidates) so the mod never destroys a block without its vanilla drops and never gives more than vanilla would.

nodes.label: D2: Vanilla-equivalent durability, drops, hunger
nodes.rationale: destroyBlockAs is given the selected stack so mineBlock/hurtAndBreak (Unbreaking), Block.getDrops (Silk Touch/Fortune) and causeFoodExhaustion(0.005F) all mirror vanilla mining exactly, keeping the feature balanced rather than a free bonus.

nodes.label: D3: Capped mining delay instead of instant breaking
nodes.norm_label: d3: capped mining delay instead of instant breaking
nodes.rationale: delay = min(maxDelayTicks, sum of estimateBreakTicks) approximates vanilla's per-tick mining progress without efficiency/haste modifiers, capped at 40 ticks (2s) by default, so mass-breaking cannot become an instant-mining exploit while staying fast enough to feel like a bulk feature.

nodes.label: D4: Existing survival limits stay in force
nodes.norm_label: d4: existing survival limits stay in force
nodes.rationale: Blocks-per-click/axis, reach by power level, maxBlocksPlacedAtOnce, allowInSurvival, whitelist and tile-entity protection remain unchanged, plus new spawn-protection/adventure-mode checks, so survival breaking does not bypass any pre-existing anti-griefing/balance limit.

nodes.label: D5: Vanilla breaking cancelled while a build mode is active (survival included)
nodes.norm_label: d5: vanilla breaking cancelled while a build mode is active (survival included)
nodes.rationale: Keeps one consistent mental model: build mode on = mod breaks with its own rules (creative and survival alike); Disable = pure vanilla. Avoids a confusing hybrid where survival players could sometimes vanilla-mine and sometimes mod-break depending on tool state.

nodes.label: D6: Client preview and HUD for break plan
nodes.norm_label: d6: client preview and hud for break plan
nodes.rationale: Entries the client cannot find a tool for are flagged invalid and drawn grey instead of red; HUD near the crosshair shows tools and per-tool block counts plus a barrier icon for unbreakable-count, so the player understands why some blocks won't break without guessing.

nodes.label: D7: ServerConfig.survivalBreaking defaults
nodes.rationale: enabled=true, stopBeforeToolBreaks=true, maxDelayTicks=40, exhaustionPerBlock=0.005, centralizing the on/off switch and tunables in one place even though SimpleConfigValue is still an in-memory-only placeholder on both loaders (no file is read yet).

nodes.label: Root cause: Disable mode client/server desync after rejoin
nodes.norm_label: root cause: disable mode client/server desync after rejoin
nodes.rationale: ServerBuildState is session-only and reset by handleNewPlayer on join, but the client's static BuildModes.buildMode field survives leaving a world and was never re-sent on join, so client and server could disagree about whether Disable mode is active after a rejoin; fixed by BuildModes.resyncToServer() sending state on ClientPlayConnectionEvents.JOIN (T-S6).

nodes.label: Root cause: survival breaking always used ItemStack.EMPTY, no correct-tool check
nodes.norm_label: root cause: survival breaking always used itemstack.empty, no correct-tool check
nodes.rationale: BlockPlacerHelper.breakBlock always called BlockHelper.destroyBlockAs with ItemStack.EMPTY: no correct-tool check, durability, silk touch/fortune, or hunger; vanilla's requiresCorrectToolForDrops enforcement happens in Block.playerDestroy, which this path never went through, so a wooden pickaxe would silently delete diamond ore with no drop unless the mod added its own check.

nodes.label: C3: RenderHandler HUD shows on pretend state, not only active breaking
nodes.norm_label: c3: renderhandler hud shows on pretend state, not only active breaking
nodes.rationale: Checking getPretendBuildingState() instead of getBuildingState() lets a survival player see the tool/barrier HUD just from looking at a block, which is how they learn why nothing would break, rather than only after they start actively breaking.

nodes.label: C4: BreakToolHelper.collectCandidates snapshot() called once instead of per-iteration
nodes.norm_label: c4: breaktoolhelper.collectcandidates snapshot() called once instead of per-iteration
nodes.rationale: Calling ClientBackpackToolCache.snapshot() (which copies the whole list) once per loop iteration plus once per ToolSlot.get() was wasteful; capturing the snapshot once before the loop and indexing into it is an efficiency cleanup with no behavioural change.

nodes.label: D8: Deliberate out-of-scope items
nodes.rationale: Automatic tool swapping into hand, inserting drops into backpacks, extra XP for delayed breaks, Disable-mode breaking beyond existing modifier behaviour, and config file loading were all excluded to keep the change scoped to the requested feature.
